bug.title: NUCC taxonomy CSV pollutes SpecialtyMetaData with codes for unlicensed humans
bug.description: The NUCC provider taxonomy CSV (loaded by Code/DataPipelines/load_specialty_data.py from nucc.org) defines codes for individual roles that are not licensed healthcare practitioners — e.g., Homemaker (376J00000X), Reflexologist (173C00000X), Driver (172A00000X), Health & Wellness Coach (171400000X), Lay Midwife (175M00000X), Funeral Director (176P00000X), Veterinarian (174M00000X), Graphics Designer (1744G0900X), Religious Nonmedical Practitioner (374K00000X), Lactation Consultant Non-RN (174N00000X), Peer Specialist (175T00000X), and 25+ others sitting in NUCC Grouping 'Other Service Providers' plus the single 'Student, Health Care' code (390200000X). All of these pass the existing $vectorSearch filter {Section: 'Individual'} in domain/find_care/specialty_service.py because Section=Individual only excludes group-practice and non-individual entries; it does NOT distinguish licensed from unlicensed roles. NUCC itself has no 'requires license' field. The result is that the specialty filter surfaces non-licensed and non-clinical roles in user-facing search results (e.g., a 'find me a foot doctor' query can return Homemaker, Reflexologist, Driver, etc.). Fix approach: derive the legitimate NUCC code set from the NPPES NPI database — query NPPES for the distinct NUCC codes actually registered against real NPIs (Type 1 individual + Type 2 organization) and use that derived set as the allow-list at pipeline load time. Every NUCC code that has at least one real NPI registrant is in scope; codes with zero NPI registrants get excluded automatically. SpecialtyMetaData may need enrichment with the NPI Type(s) per NUCC code. False negatives are acceptable — every legitimate NUCC code will have at least one NPI record. A new pipeline requirement is needed and will be authored on 2026-05-04.
bug.reproduction: 1. Connect to {env}_PublicHealthData.SpecialtyMetaData. 2. Query: db.SpecialtyMetaData.find({Section:'Individual', Grouping: {$in: ['Other Service Providers', 'Student, Health Care']}}).count() — observe 37 records present in the dev cluster. 3. Run a specialty search via the specialty filter (e.g., 'find me a foot doctor'); observe non-licensed/non-clinical entries (Homemaker, Reflexologist, Driver, etc.) appearing in vector-search results.
next_action: The list of legitimate clinical NUCC codes MUST be curated manually. The NPPES-derived allow-list approach was tried (is_npi_registered field on ProprietaryData.SpecialtyAndProviderFlags, populated 2026-05-24) and found insufficient: 821 of 883 catalog codes have NPI registrants in our 298K-provider sample, including the polluting codes (Homemaker 376J00000X, Reflexologist 173C00000X, Driver 172A00000X) — real people DO register their NPI under these codes. A curated allow/deny list is the only reliable discriminator.

bug.title: Incremental load never deletes records missing from a full source file
bug.description:
EPIC-010-F-007-S-004-REQ-B-002 says: when `incremental=true`, no provider record shall be deleted or altered unless (a) the source row changed (record altered to match), or (b) the source is a full file and the record is missing from it (record deleted).

The implementation only does (a). When `incremental=true`, `pipeline/Code/provider_load_manager.py:231-235` skips drain entirely, and `pipeline/Code/provider_worker.py:345-367` upserts each present row by NPI via `ReplaceOne({"npi": npi}, doc, upsert=True)`. There is NO post-load reconciliation pass that detects NPIs in the collection but missing from the source file and deletes them.

NPPES is always a full dissemination file when the monthly file is used, so REQ branch (b) applies on every full-file incremental run, but no code path implements it. Stale and CMS-retired NPIs accumulate indefinitely in incremental mode.
test_success_criteria: An `incremental=true` run against an NPPES dissemination file MUST delete every provider record whose NPI is not present in the source file.
Boolean test: pre-load count = N, source file count = N - K (K NPIs missing), post-load count = N - K, and the K specific NPIs are no longer in the collection.
bug.reproduction:
1. Run a full load of state X with `incremental=false` - collection holds 1000 NPIs for X.
2. Wait one NPPES dissemination cycle in which CMS retires/merges 50 of those NPIs.
3. Operator runs `incremental=true`. Two source-file paths exist:
   3.a. Weekly NPPES incremental file: contains only records that changed since last weekly/full. The 50 retired NPIs appear in the diff with their NPI Deactivation Date populated. The code upserts each present row by NPI via `ReplaceOne({"npi": npi}, doc, upsert=True)`. The deactivation date is stored on the document but no logic acts on it: no out_of_scope flag is set, no record is deleted, no downstream signal is emitted. (REQ-B-002 branch (b) does not apply here because the source is not a full file; this exposes an orthogonal deactivation-flag-handling gap, and the system has no enforced way to distinguish weekly vs full source.)
   3.b. Monthly NPPES full file: contains every currently-disseminated record (active + deactivated-but-not-yet-purged); long-retired NPIs are absent entirely (CMS-purged). The code only upserts rows present in the file. There is NO post-load pass that scans the collection for NPIs absent from the source file. Long-retired (CMS-purged) NPIs remain in the collection indefinitely; recently-deactivated NPIs (still in the file with deactivation dates) remain 'active' in collection state. Direct violation of REQ-B-002 branch (b).
4. FindCare search returns providers CMS has retired.
next_action: If a real business need to use incremental loading arises (currently every load is full), this bug must be fixed before the first incremental run.
Until then, all loads are `incremental=false` (drain -> reload), which is correct behavior under REQ-B-002 for full-loads and avoids the gap entirely.

V8 req capturing branch (b) of the legacy REQ-B-002 (full-source-file -> delete DB records absent from source) does NOT exist in EPIC-010-F-102-S-005. A new requirement under F-102-S-005 MUST be authored to capture this delete-on-absence semantic before this bug can be re-attached.

bug.title: Deploy build context ships files that no runtime code path uses
bug.description: It is required that our deployment scripts deploy exactly what is needed to each target — no more, no less. Today that requirement is not met for files: extraneous source files ship to targets where no runtime code path on that target imports or reads them. The reverse direction — artifacts required by deployed code that are not declared in the manifest — is captured by REQ-B-008 for env vars and REQ-B-009 for entitlements; both are approved and 'done' on S-001 with the substrate already in the schema. Why this matters: our runtime architecture is documented in deployment_architecture.json and nowhere else. As long as the manifest carries garbage (files that nothing on the target uses), no process — human or automated — can extract the actual architecture from it, and the firm continues to operate with undocumented architecture. Surfacing example: architecture/DevOpsBuildDeployAndEnvironmentManagement/hf_helpers.py:_findcare_source_set returns ('Code/Shared', 'Code/Shared') as one of the subtrees wholesale-copied into the FindCare HF build context by _copy_tree, which recursively copies every file under it. Code/Shared/ops/ is dev-time / planning-time tooling (promote_data.py, bump_build.py, seed_versions_collection.py, unattended_monitor.py, local_admin_server.py, sync_to_mongo.py, and — until 2026-06-04 — manifest_generator.py and epic_planning_runner.py) with no runtime caller in the FindCare backend. These files ride along into every FindCare HF deploy as dead bytes. The disposition: 'referenced' tag in deployment_architecture.json under target_hf_space_findcare_backend does NOT gate shipping — it is a content-hash audit trail only; what ships is determined by the subtree walk. EvaluateCare and SharedServices source sets do not include Code/Shared, so this specific symptom is FindCare-only, but the structural pattern (build context driven by wholesale subtree-copy rather than by an explicit per-target file list in the manifest) applies wherever the same mechanism is used.
test_success_criteria: Every file present in a target's build context is reached by a runtime code path on that target. No file present in a build context is unused by the runtime that target hosts.
bug.reproduction: 1. Run local_build --target findcare. 2. Inspect the build_dir's Code/Shared/ops/ subdirectory; observe every file currently in repo Code/Shared/ops/ (minus standard excludes) is present. 3. Grep the FindCare backend (Code/ConversationalUX/FindCareChat/backend/, FindCare/, FrontEndApplicationLib/) for imports of any module under Code/Shared/ops/. Observe: zero hits. The files are dead bytes shipped to HF on every deploy.
next_action: Author a new REQ on EPIC-008-F-012-S-001 capturing the bidirectional exact-truth contract for files per target — analog to REQ-B-008 (env vars) and REQ-B-009 (entitlements). Re-link this bug's req_id when the REQ exists.
Replace the wholesale subtree-copy mechanism with an explicit per-target file list driven by deployment_architecture.json. The build stages only what the manifest enumerates for that target.
Implement, then bring this bug to closed.
